    66	/-- The (possibly unnormalized) rank-one state associated to a Euclidean vector. -/
    67	private noncomputable def vectorQuantumState {ι : Type*}
    68	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    69	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : QuantumState ι where
    70	  density := pureDensity ψ.ofLp
    71	  density_psd := by
    72	    refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_

    76	/-- Evaluation in the rank-one vector state is the corresponding quadratic form. -/
    77	private theorem vectorQuantumState_ev_eq_stateQForm {ι : Type*}
    78	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    79	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (T : Op ι) :
    80	    ev (vectorQuantumState ψ) T = stateQForm ψ T := by
    81	  have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) ≠ 0 :=
    82	    Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
    83	  change (MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (pureDensity ψ.ofLp * T)).re =
    84	    stateQForm ψ T
    85	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_mul_comm]
    86	  unfold pureDensity MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
    87	  rw [Matrix.mul_smul, Matrix.mul_vecMulVec, Matrix.trace_smul, Matrix.trace_vecMulVec]
    88	  change (((Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
    89	      ((T *ᵥ ψ.ofLp) ⬝ᵥ star ψ.ofLp)) /
    90	      (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)).re = stateQForm ψ T

   315	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   316	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   317	  open Classical in
   318	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   319	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   320	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   321	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   322	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   327	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   328	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   329	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   330	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   331	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   332	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   333	      else false

   184	/-- Bipartite questionwise consistency defect.
   185	
   186	In the paper (Definition 4.8), the consistency of `A` on `H_A` and `B` on
   187	`H_B` for a shared state `|ψ⟩ ∈ H_A ⊗ H_B` is:
   188	  `E_x ∑_{a≠b} ⟨ψ| A^x_a ⊗ B^x_b |ψ⟩ ≤ δ`
   189	which equals
   190	  `max 0 (⟨ψ| A_total ⊗ B_total |ψ⟩ − ∑_a ⟨ψ| A_a ⊗ B_a |ψ⟩)`. -/
   191	noncomputable def qBipartiteConsDefect {Outcome : Type*}
   192	    {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   193	    [Fintype Outcome]
   194	    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB))
   195	    (A : SubMeas Outcome ιA) (B : SubMeas Outcome ιB) : Error :=
   196	  let totalOverlap := ev ψ (opTensor A.total B.total)
   197	  max 0 (totalOverlap - qBipartiteMatchMass ψ A B)

1	\section{Classical and Quantum Low-degree Tests}
     2	\label{sec:ldt}
     3	
     4	In this section we introduce the classical and quantum low individual degree tests, that form the basis of our classical, quantum-sound and quantum PCP constructions. For quantum soundness of the classical test we refer to~\cite{ML20}. For the quantum test, we refer to~\cite{natarajan2018low} and its adaptation to the low individual degree test given in Appendix~\ref{sec:qld-analysis}. 
     5	The protocol in this work combines both of these tests, using the quantum
     6	low individual degree test for question reduction and the classical low individual degree test for
     7	answer reduction.
     8	Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier} below introduces the classical test,
     9	and Section~\ref{sec:pauli-verifier} does the same for the quantum 
    10	test.
    11	Prior to doing this, we introduce the \emph{Magic Square game} in
    12	Section~\ref{sec:ms}, a key subroutine in the quantum test.
    13	
    14	
    15	\subsection{The classical low-degree test}
    16	\label{sec:ld-verifier}
    17	
    18	We begin with a generalization of the classical low-degree test known as the
    19	``simultaneous individual low-degree test''.
    20	We sometimes refer to this as the ``classical low-degree test'' for short.
    21	The low-degree test is used as a subroutine in the Pauli Basis test (see
    22	Section~\ref{sec:pauli-verifier}) as well as the answer-reduction normal form
    23	verifier (see Section~\ref{sec:ans}).
    24	We describe the test as a nonlocal game in Section~\ref{sec:ld-game} and show
    25	that the question distribution can be implemented as a (typed) conditionally
    26	linear distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL
    27	distributions).
    28	
    29	
    30	\subsubsection{The game}
    31	\label{sec:ld-game}
    32	
    33	The game $\game^\ld$ is parametrized by a tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
    34	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
    35	and $m$ divides $q$.
    36	We sometimes write $\game^\ld_\ldparams$ to emphasize the dependence of the
    37	classical low-degree test on the parameter tuple $\ldparams$.
    38	
    39	We first provide a high-level description of the game for $k=1$.
    40	It is based on the low-individual degree variant of the multilinearity test
    41	of~\cite{babai1991non}, where one player (called the ``points player'') receives
    42	a random point $u \in \F_q^m$, and the other player (called the ``lines
    43	player'') receives a random axis-parallel line $\line$ that contains $u$, i.e.\
    44	the line parallel to the $i$-th axis which goes through point $u$, for uniformly
    45	random $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$.
    46	The points player is supposed to respond with a value $a \in \F_q$, and the
    47	lines player is supposed to respond with a univariate polynomial $f_\line$ of
    48	degree at most $d$ such that $f_\line(u_i) = a$, where $u_i$ is the $i$-th
    49	coordinate of $u$.
    50	
    51	Suppose the players agree beforehand on a global polynomial $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$
    52	such that every variable has degree at most $d$.
    53	Then a winning strategy is the following: the points player responds with
    54	$g(u)$, and the lines player responds with the univariate polynomial $f_\line$
    55	that is the restriction of $g$ to line $\line$; formally, for $t \in \F_q$,
    56	\[f_\line(t)=g(u_1,u_2,\ldots,u_{i-1},t,u_{i+1},\ldots,u_m)\;.\] It is easy to
    57	see that $f_\line(t)$ has degree at most $d$ in the variable $t$.
    58	Thus in this case the players will pass the low-degree test with probability
    59	$1$.
    60	The low-degree testing theorem states that the converse approximately holds: if
    61	the players pass the low-degree test with probability close to $1$, then their
    62	responses must be approximately consistent (in some sense) with a global
    63	polynomial $g$ with individual degree $d$.
    64	
    65	When $k > 1$, the players are supposed to respond with a \emph{tuple} of
    66	answers; and the test is intended to check that the players' responses are
    67	consistent with a $k$-tuple of functions $g_i: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ that are
    68	polynomials where every variable has degree at most $d$.
    69	
    70	The game that we use is slightly more elaborate than the ``axis-parallel
    71	lines-versus-points'' test just described.
    72	In addition, we have two other subtests.
    73	One is a ``diagonal line-vs-points'' test: here, the points player receives a
    74	point $u \in \F_q^m$ as before, but the lines player receives a line $\line$
    75	that goes through $u$ but is not necessarily axis-aligned.
    76	Instead, it's chosen by first picking an index $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$
    77	uniformly at random, picking $v \in \F_q^m$ uniformly at random, and letting $v'
    78	= \pi_{i-1}(v) = (0,0,\ldots,0,v_i,v_{i+1},\ldots,v_m)$ (i.e., $\pi_{i-1}$
    79	zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of its input).
    80	Then, the line is defined as the set
    81	\[
    82		\line = \{ u + tv' : t \in \F_q \}\;,
    83	\]
    84	which is a uniformly random line in the affine subspace of $\F^m_q$
    85	corresponding to all points $v$ whose first $(i-1)$ coordinates match those of
    86	$u$.
    87	The points player responds with a value $a \in \F_q$, the lines player responds
    88	with a univariate polynomial $f_\line$ of degree $md$,\footnote{Since $\line$ is
    89	  no longer axis-parallel, the restriction of an individual degree-$d$
    90	  polynomial $g$ to a line $\line$ may yield a degree $md$ polynomial.}
    91	and the verifier checks that $f_\line(t_u) = a$ (where $t_u \in \F_q$ is the
    92	projection of $u$ onto the line $\line$ with respect to a canonical
    93	parameterization of $\line$).
    94	
    95	The other additional test is a ``consistency test'', where both players receive
    96	either the same points question, the same axis-parallel lines question, or the
    97	same diagonal lines question.
    98	In all cases they are expected to respond with the same answer.
    99	
   100	
   101	
   102	\paragraph{Axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines.}
   103	Before presenting a formal description of the game $\game^\ld$, we first define
   104	what we mean by lines, and their properties.
   105	
   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.
   238	
   239	
   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}
   258	
   259	
   260	
   261	\begin{lemma}
   262		\label{lem:dlnf}
   263		Consider the pair $(\line,u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   264	  tuple $((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$,
   265	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,v)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   266	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a random
   267	  diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares the first $i-1$ coordinates
   268	  with $u$, for uniformly random $i$.
   269	\end{lemma}
   270	\begin{proof}
   271		The proof of this follows identically to \Cref{lem:alnf}.
   272	\end{proof}

   274	For later convenience we make the following definition. 
   275	
   276	\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]
   277	        \label{def:line-point-dist}
   278	 The \emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\ALine}$ is the
   279	 distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$ over pairs $(\ell=(u_0,e_i),u)$
   280	 (we omit the $0$ elements for simplicity). The \emph{diagonal
   281	   line-point distribution} $D_{\DLine}$ is the distribution
   282	 $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$  over $(\ell=(u_0,s,v),u)$. The
   283	 \emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\Line}$ is the equal mixture of the axis-parallel line-point distribution and the diagonal line-point distribution.
   284	 In other words, a sample from $D_{\Line}$ is distributed as follows:
   285	 with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\ALine}$,
   286	 and with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\DLine}$.
   287	\end{definition}

   320	\paragraph{Decision procedure} The decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ for the
   321	game $\game^\ld$ is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}.
   322	The table at the top specifies a parsing scheme for the questions and answers,
   323	depending on the type of question.
   324	For example, when a player receives a question with type $\Point$, the question
   325	content $x$, a bit string of length $m \log q$, should be interpreted by the
   326	decision procedure and the players as an element of the vector space $\F_q^m$,
   327	as indicated in Section~\ref{sec:ff-representations}.
   328	Similarly the answer to a question with type $\Point$ is expected to be a bit
   329	string of length $\ldc \log q$, and is interpreted as an element of $\F_q^\ldc$.
   330	For questions with type $\ALine$, the question content is a $(m \log q + \log
   331	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a pair $(u_0, s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$,
   332	which in turn can be interpreted as a specification for an axis-parallel line
   333	$\line(u_0,e_i)$ in $\F_q^m$ where $i = \chi(s)$, as described in
   334	\Cref{lem:alnf}.
   335	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$d$ univariate
   336	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,e_i)$, each polynomial given by a
   337	list of $d+1$ coefficients.
   338	For questions with type $\DLine$, the question content is a $(2m \log q + \log
   339	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a triple $(u_0, s, v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q
   340	\times \F_q^m$ that specifies a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ where $v' =
   341	\pi_{i-1}(v)$ as described in \Cref{lem:dlnf}.
   342	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$md$ univariate
   343	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,v')$.
   344	If the answers returned by the players do not fit this format the decision
   345	procedure rejects.

    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    31	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    32	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    33	`def:ld-game` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    36	-/
    37	structure LdParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  k : ℕ
    42	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    43	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    44	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    45	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    46	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    47	
    48	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    49	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    50	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    51	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    52	
    53	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    54	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    55	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    57	-/
    58	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    59	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    60	
    61	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    62	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    63	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    65	-/
    66	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    67	
    68	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    69	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    70	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    71	-/
    72	inductive LdType where
    73	  | point
    74	  | aline
    75	  | dline
    76	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    77	
    78	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    79	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    80	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    81	-/
    82	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    83	
    84	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    85	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    87	-/
    88	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    89	
    90	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    91	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    92	-/
    93	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    94	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    95	
    96	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    97	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    98	-/
    99	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   100	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   101	
   102	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   103	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   104	-/
   105	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   106	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   107	
   108	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   109	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   110	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   112	-/
   113	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   114	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   115	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   116	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   117	
   118	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   119	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   120	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   121	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   122	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   123	-/
   124	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   125	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   126	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   127	
   128	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   129	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   130	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   132	-/
   133	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   134	  fun i => match i with
   135	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   136	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   137	  | .inr _ => 0
   138	
   139	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   140	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   141	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   142	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   143	-/
   144	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   145	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   146	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   147	  fun i => match i with
   148	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   149	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   150	  | .inr _ => 0
   195	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   196	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   197	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   198	-/
   199	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   200	
   201	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   202	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   203	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   204	-/
   205	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   206	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   207	  Distribution.map
   208	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   209	    (fun s =>
   210	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   211	
   212	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   213	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   214	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   215	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   216	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   217	-/
   218	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   219	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   220	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   221	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   222	  deriving DecidableEq
   223	
   224	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   225	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   226	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   227	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   228	-/
   229	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   230	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   231	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   232	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   233	
   234	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   235	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   236	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   237	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   238	-/
   239	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   240	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   241	  toFun
   242	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   243	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   244	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   245	  invFun
   246	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   247	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   248	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   249	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   250	  right_inv := by
   251	    intro x
   252	    cases x with
   253	    | inl a => rfl
   254	    | inr x =>
   255	        cases x with
   256	        | inl a => rfl
   257	        | inr a => rfl
   258	
   259	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   260	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   261	
   262	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   263	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   264	
   265	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   266	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   267	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   268	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   269	-/
   270	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   271	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   272	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   273	
   274	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   275	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   276	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   277	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   278	-/
   279	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   280	  match t, a with
   281	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   282	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   283	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   284	  | _, _ => false
   285	
   286	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   287	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   288	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   289	-/
   290	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   291	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   292	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   293	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   294	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   295	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   296	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   297	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   298	
   299	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   302	-/
   303	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   304	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   305	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   306	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   307	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   308	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   309	
   310	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   311	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   312	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   313	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   314	-/
   315	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   316	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   317	  open Classical in
   318	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   319	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   320	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   321	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   322	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   327	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   328	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   329	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   330	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   331	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   332	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   333	      else false
   334	
   335	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   336	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   337	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   338	-/
   339	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   340	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   341	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   342	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   343	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   344	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   345	  μ_prob := (uniformDistribution_isProbability
   346	    ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)).map _
   347	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   348	
   349	end

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:18:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldGame}

    29	/-- A uniform consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of

    31	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv
    32	    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}
    33	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    34	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    35	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    36	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    37	    (e : X ≃ Y) (A B : Y → Outcome → Op iota)
    38	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    39	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
    40	        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =
    41	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
    42	  unfold consistencyDefect
    43	  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : Outcome, ∑ b : Outcome,
    45	      if a = b then 0 else
    46	        (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    47	          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)
    48	
    49	/-- A consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of both
    50	outcome families. -/

    52	    {X Alpha Beta iota : Type*}

    54	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
    55	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
    56	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    57	    (mu : Distribution X) (e : Beta ≃ Alpha)
    58	    (A B : X → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    59	    consistencyDefect mu
    60	        (fun x b => A x (e b)) (fun x b => B x (e b)) psi =
    61	      consistencyDefect mu A B psi := by
    62	  unfold consistencyDefect
    63	  apply avgOver_congr
    64	  intro x
    65	  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>
    66	    if a = b then 0 else
    67	      (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    68	        (((A x a) * (B x b)).mulVec psi))).re
    69	  calc
    70	    _ = ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Beta, term (e a) (e b) := by
    71	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    72	      intro a _
    73	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    74	      intro b _

    76	      by_cases hab : a = b

    86	    _ = ∑ a : Alpha, ∑ b : Alpha, term a b :=
    87	      Equiv.sum_comp e (fun a => ∑ b : Alpha, term a b)

    59	\section{Key theorem forms}
    60	
    61	Throughout, $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
    62	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
    63	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
    64	over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
    65	theorem forms.
    66	\begin{enumerate}
    67	  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
    68	  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
    69	  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
    70	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
    71	  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
    72	  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
    73	  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
    74	  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
    75	  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
    76	  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
    77	  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
    78	  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
    79	  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
    80	  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
    81	  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
    82	  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
    83	  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
    84	  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
    85	  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.
    86	  \item \textbf{Restricted form supported by the present route.}  The source
    87	  theorem form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among
    88	  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and
    89	  $q \ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ and for
    90	  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.
    91	  \item \textbf{Repaired import form} (recommended target).  Quantum
    92	  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual
    93	  degree game over $\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \ge 1$ and
    94	  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question
    95	  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,
    96	  uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly rather than through an index
    97	  function on $\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in
    98	  place of the seed $s \in \F_q$; the error is
    99	  $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m',d,k) = a(dm'k)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} +
   100	  2^{-bm'd})$.  This is a candidate target form, not an established one:
   101	  proving it carries the same two import obligations as the $\chi$-based
   102	  import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), and deriving the present
   103	  form from it when $m' \mid q$ requires the strategy transport described
   104	  under the candidate repairs below, whose synchronicity step is an open
   105	  obligation.
   106	\end{enumerate}

   108	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   109	
   110	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   111	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   112	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   113	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   114	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   115	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   116	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   117	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   118	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   119	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   120	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   121	proof, and admissibility are at
   122	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   123	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   124	There, the combined point measurements
   125	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   126	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   127	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   128	individual degree game with parameters
   129	\[
   130	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   131	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   132	\]
   133	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   134	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   135	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   136	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   137	
   138	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   139	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   140	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   141	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   142	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   143	$\chi(s)$ with
   144	\[
   145	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   146	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   147	\]
   148	so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
   149	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   150	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.
   151	
   152	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   153	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   154	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   155	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   156	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   157	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   158	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   159	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility, so its proof route
   160	establishes the polynomial-pair lemma, and with it the soundness theorem for
   161	the Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.
   162	
   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}

   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint

   211	/-- Postprocessing is functorial: postprocessing by `f` and then by `g`

   213	@[simp] theorem postprocess_comp {α β γ : Type*} {ι : Type*}

1	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap

/-!
# Question and answer transport for the directly indexed low-degree game

This module reads mature low individual degree questions as canonical direct
questions and rebases direct answers to the mature line parametrization.

Points and lines are decoded with the coordinate order reversed
(`directPointEquiv`), so that the suffix-zero direction restriction of the
mature diagonal test becomes the prefix-zero restriction of the direct game.
A mature diagonal line reveals no coordinate index, whereas a direct diagonal
question carries one.  The transported question uses the *leading index* of
the decoded direction, the least coordinate at which the direction is
nonzero.  Under the direct sampler, this is the index attached to the sampled
direction exactly when the direction is nonzero at the sampled index
(`directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection`), an event of conditional
probability `1 - 1/q`; on the mature side, the leading index of a decoded
`j`-restricted direction is `Fin.rev j` exactly when its pivot coordinate is
nonzero (`directDiagonalIndexOf_extendRestrictedDirection`).  Diagonal answers
on zero-direction lines are read as the constant polynomial carrying their
value at the base point, following `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.

- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:230-272`

- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:120-121`

1	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap
   165	
   166	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

   111	    (htotal : A.total = B.total) :
   112	    A = B := by
   113	  cases A with
   114	  | mk outcomeA totalA posA sumA leA =>
   115	      cases B with
   116	      | mk outcomeB totalB posB sumB leB =>
   117	          have houtcome' : outcomeA = outcomeB := by
   118	            funext a
   119	            exact houtcome a
   120	          cases houtcome'
   121	          cases htotal
   122	          cases Subsingleton.elim posB posA
   123	          cases Subsingleton.elim sumB sumA
   124	          cases Subsingleton.elim leB leA
   125	          rfl

   128	@[ext] theorem Measurement.ext {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   129	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   130	    {A B : Measurement α ι}
   131	    (houtcome : ∀ a : α, A.outcome a = B.outcome a) :
   132	    A = B := by
   133	  cases A with
   134	  | mk AtoSubMeas AtotalEqOne =>
   135	      cases B with
   136	      | mk BtoSubMeas BtotalEqOne =>
   137	          have hsub : AtoSubMeas = BtoSubMeas := by

   145	          cases Subsingleton.elim BtotalEqOne AtotalEqOne

   149	operators. -/

   151	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   152	    {A B : ProjMeas α ι}

    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)

    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,

     4	# Low-degree consistency defect transport
     5	
     6	This module reindexes the QPBT consistency defect and transports the three
     7	consistency conclusions of the mature low individual degree theorem without
     8	changing their numerical bounds.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:393-458`
    13	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`
    14	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

    26	
    27	/-! ## Reindexing the QPBT defect -/
    28	
    29	/-- A uniform consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of
    30	its question type. -/
    31	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv
    32	    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}
    33	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    34	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    35	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    36	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    37	    (e : X ≃ Y) (A B : Y → Outcome → Op iota)
    38	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    39	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
    40	        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =
    41	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
    42	  unfold consistencyDefect
    43	  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : Outcome, ∑ b : Outcome,
    45	      if a = b then 0 else
    46	        (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    47	          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)
    48	
    49	/-- A consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of both
    50	outcome families. -/
    51	theorem consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv
    52	    {X Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    53	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    54	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
    55	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
    56	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    57	    (mu : Distribution X) (e : Beta ≃ Alpha)
    58	    (A B : X → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    59	    consistencyDefect mu
    60	        (fun x b => A x (e b)) (fun x b => B x (e b)) psi =
    61	      consistencyDefect mu A B psi := by
    62	  unfold consistencyDefect
    63	  apply avgOver_congr
    64	  intro x
    65	  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>
    66	    if a = b then 0 else
    67	      (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    68	        (((A x a) * (B x b)).mulVec psi))).re
    69	  calc
    70	    _ = ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Beta, term (e a) (e b) := by
    71	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    72	      intro a _
    73	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    74	      intro b _
    75	      unfold term
    76	      by_cases hab : a = b
    77	      · subst b
    78	        simp
    79	      · have heab : e a ≠ e b := fun h => hab (e.injective h)
    80	        simp [hab, heab]
    81	    _ =
    82	        ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Alpha, term (e a) b := by
    83	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    84	      intro a _
    85	      exact Equiv.sum_comp e (fun b => term (e a) b)
    86	    _ = ∑ a : Alpha, ∑ b : Alpha, term a b :=
    87	      Equiv.sum_comp e (fun a => ∑ b : Alpha, term a b)
    88	    _ = _ := rfl
    89	
    90	/-- Simultaneous bijective relabeling of uniform questions and outcomes leaves
    91	the consistency defect unchanged. -/
    92	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_outcome_equiv
    93	    {X Y Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    94	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    95	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    96	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
    97	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
    98	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    99	    (questionEquiv : X ≃ Y) (outcomeEquiv : Beta ≃ Alpha)
   100	    (A B : Y → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   101	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   102	        (fun x b => A (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b))
   103	        (fun x b => B (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b)) psi =
   104	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
   105	  calc
   106	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   107	        (fun x b => A (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b))
   108	        (fun x b => B (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b)) psi =
   109	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   110	        (fun x a => A (questionEquiv x) a)
   111	        (fun x a => B (questionEquiv x) a) psi :=
   112	      consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv (uniformDistribution X)
   113	        outcomeEquiv _ _ psi
   114	    _ = consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi :=
   115	      consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv questionEquiv A B psi

   117	/-! ## The three mature LDT conclusions in direct coordinates -/
   118	
   119	/-- Pointwise equality of both operator families gives equality of their
   120	consistency defects. -/
   121	theorem consistencyDefect_congr
   122	    {X Outcome iota : Type*}
   123	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
   124	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
   125	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   126	    (mu : Distribution X) (A A' B B' : X → Outcome → Op iota)
   127	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota)
   128	    (hA : ∀ x a, A x a = A' x a) (hB : ∀ x a, B x a = B' x a) :
   129	    consistencyDefect mu A B psi = consistencyDefect mu A' B' psi := by
   130	  unfold consistencyDefect
   131	  apply avgOver_congr
   132	  intro x
   133	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   134	  intro a _
   135	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   136	  intro b _
   137	  by_cases hab : a = b
   138	  · simp [hab]
   139	  · simp only [hab, if_false]
   140	    rw [hA x a, hB x b]
   141	
   142	/-- The direct single-coordinate point/global defect is exactly the mature

   144	theorem directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq

   153	          (fun u a => heteroKron 1
   154	            ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a)) S.ψ =
   155	        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))

     5	/-!

     7	
     8	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     9	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
    10	operator algebra.  The observable/projector expansions are obtained from
    11	finite-field Fourier orthogonality in characteristic two.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    16	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    27	
    28	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    29	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    30	
    31	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    32	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    34	-/
    35	inductive PauliKind where
    36	  | X
    37	  | Z
    38	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    39	
    40	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    41	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    42	
    43	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    44	character in their statement types. -/
    45	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    46	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    47	
    48	/-- In characteristic two, the standard additive character is the sign
    49	character used by the binary Pauli definitions. -/
    50	theorem phaseSign_eq_ffChar (t : ZMod 2) :
    51	    phaseSign t = ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2) t := by
    52	  by_cases ht : t = 0
    53	  · subst t
    54	    rw [phaseSign, if_pos rfl]
    55	    exact (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2)).map_zero_eq_one.symm
    56	  · have hval : t.val = 1 := by
    57	      have hval_ne : t.val ≠ 0 := (ZMod.val_ne_zero t).mpr ht
    58	      have hval_lt : t.val < 2 := ZMod.val_lt t
    59	      omega
    60	    have ht_one : t = 1 := (ZMod.val_eq_one (by omega) t).mp hval
    61	    subst t
    62	    rw [phaseSign, if_neg one_ne_zero]
    63	    change (-1 : ℂ) = ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2) ((1 : ℤ) : ZMod 2)
    64	    rw [ZMod.stdAddChar_coe]
    65	    convert Complex.exp_pi_mul_I.symm using 1
    66	    all_goals ring_nf
    67	
    68	private theorem phaseSign_add (s t : ZMod 2) :
    69	    phaseSign (s + t) = phaseSign s * phaseSign t := by
    70	  rw [phaseSign_eq_ffChar, phaseSign_eq_ffChar, phaseSign_eq_ffChar]
    71	  exact (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := 2)).map_add_eq_mul s t
    72	
    73	private theorem star_phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : star (phaseSign t) = phaseSign t := by
    74	  by_cases ht : t = 0 <;> simp [phaseSign, ht]
    75	
    76	/-- The binary sign character sends sums to products. -/
    77	theorem phaseSign_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → ZMod 2) :
    78	    phaseSign (∑ i, f i) = ∏ i, phaseSign (f i) := by

    81	  | empty => simp [phaseSign]
    82	  | @insert i s hi ih =>
    83	      rw [Finset.sum_insert hi, Finset.prod_insert hi, phaseSign_add, ih]

    86	/-- The product of the coordinate phases is the phase of the trace pairing. -/
    87	theorem prod_phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]

    89	    ∏ i, phaseSign (binTrace K (u i * v i)) =
    90	      phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct u v)) := by
    91	  rw [← phaseSign_sum]
    92	  congr 2

of the decoded diagonal direction, together with answer readouts that are

conditions of `ProjStrat`.  The module also records exact Born-weight
formulas for both directions of strategy transport.

/-!
# Projective consistency evaluation

This module contains the data-processing lemmas which turn polynomial-level
projective consistency into pointwise consistency after evaluation at a sampled
point.

/-- A constant full-polynomial consistency statement postprocesses to pointwise
polynomial evaluation with the same error.

This is the data-processing move used after paper line 156: once
`Q^A_g \otimes I \simeq I \otimes Q^B_g` is available over the single
polynomial question, evaluating both polynomial outcomes at a point `u` preserves
consistency over the uniform point distribution. -/

    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
    (A B : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι) {δ : Error}
    (h : ConsRel ψ (uniformDistribution Unit)
      (constSubMeasFamily A.toSubMeas)
      (constSubMeasFamily B.toSubMeas) δ) :
    ConsRel ψ (uniformDistribution (Point params))
      (polynomialEvaluationFamily params A.toSubMeas)
      (polynomialEvaluationFamily params B.toSubMeas) δ := by
  classical
  let Aconst : IdxSubMeas (Point params) (Polynomial params) ι := fun _ => A.toSubMeas
  let Bconst : IdxSubMeas (Point params) (Polynomial params) ι := fun _ => B.toSubMeas
  have hconstPoint :
      ConsRel ψ (uniformDistribution (Point params)) Aconst Bconst δ := by
    rcases h with ⟨hbound⟩
    constructor
    have hpoint_avg :
        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Point params))
            (fun _ : Point params => qBipartiteConsDefect ψ A.toSubMeas B.toSubMeas) =
          qBipartiteConsDefect ψ A.toSubMeas B.toSubMeas := by
      haveI : Nonempty (Point params) := by infer_instance
      simpa using
        (avgOver_uniform_const (α := Point params)
          (qBipartiteConsDefect ψ A.toSubMeas B.toSubMeas))
    have hunit_eq :
        bipartiteConsError ψ (uniformDistribution Unit)
            (constSubMeasFamily A.toSubMeas) (constSubMeasFamily B.toSubMeas) =
          qBipartiteConsDefect ψ A.toSubMeas B.toSubMeas := by
      have hunit_avg :
          avgOver (uniformDistribution Unit)
              (fun _ : Unit => qBipartiteConsDefect ψ A.toSubMeas B.toSubMeas) =

        simpa using

            (qBipartiteConsDefect ψ A.toSubMeas B.toSubMeas))
